answer: Local sensor witness rotation. Each identity must answer a short challenge using a co-located environmental sensor whose readings encode site-specific conditions, such as karst drainage patterns, and submit within a rotating window. At the network nadir, challenges are issued at random intervals, so one device cannot cover many identities. Every identity requires a distinct powered sensor at a distinct site; attackers pay hardware, installation, and continuous maintenance per identity, plus failed checks when a dune shift or sensor drift breaks the match.
